senses.definition: An important subject or problem that people are discussing or arguing about.
examples: Housing was the main issue at the debate.
Let us deal with the safety issues first.
Money is not the issue here; time is.

senses.definition: To officially give out or announce something.
examples: The embassy issued a warning to travellers.
Each employee is issued with a security pass.

note: Stress falls on the second syllable in British English and the first in American English.

senses.definition: A room or building equipped for scientific experiments, research, or teaching.
examples: The samples were sent to an independent laboratory.
She runs a laboratory studying sleep and memory.
No food or drink is allowed in the laboratory.

senses.definition: Time when you are free from work or duties and can do what you enjoy.
examples: He reads history in his leisure time.
The town has invested heavily in leisure facilities.
Read the contract at your leisure and call me next week.

senses.definition: According to the exact meaning of the words, without exaggeration or metaphor.
examples: The word 'algebra' comes from Arabic and literally means 'reunion of broken parts'.
He was literally the last person to leave the building.

note: The American form usually ends in a reduced vowel; the British form keeps a full /aɪ/.

senses.definition: Able to move or be moved easily from place to place.
examples: The clinic runs a mobile unit that visits villages.
After the operation she was mobile within a week.

senses.definition: A telephone you can carry with you (chiefly British; Americans say 'cell phone').
examples: My mobile is out of battery.
Give me a call on my mobile when you land.

senses.definition: Needed in order for something to happen or be achieved.
examples: Take whatever equipment is necessary for the trip.
It is not necessary to book in advance.
She made the necessary arrangements in a single afternoon.

senses.definition: Not one nor the other of two people or things.
examples: Neither candidate convinced the panel.
Neither of the doors was locked.

senses.definition: Used to show that a negative statement is also true of someone or something else.
examples: I have not read it, and neither has she.
He could not swim, and neither could his brother.

note: British English keeps the /j/ after /n/; American English drops it.

senses.definition: Relating to the energy released when the nucleus of an atom is split or joined.
examples: The country gets a third of its electricity from nuclear power.
Both sides agreed to resume nuclear disarmament talks.
The plant's nuclear reactor was shut down for maintenance.

note: The spelling pronunciation with an audible /t/ (ˈɒf.tən, ˈɑːf.tən) is common in both varieties.

examples: We often walk along the river after supper.
How often do the buses run on Sundays?
She does not write often, but her letters are long.

senses.definition: An occasion or situation that makes it possible to do something you want to do.
examples: The fellowship gave her the opportunity to work abroad.
I would like to take this opportunity to thank the volunteers.
Do not miss the opportunity to ask questions at the end.
